title: Bomb Enemy
summary: Given an m x n matrix grid with cells as walls 'W', enemies 'E', or empty '0', determine the maximum number of enemies that can be killed by placing one bomb in an empty cell.
statement: Given an m x n matrix grid with cells as walls 'W', enemies 'E', or empty '0', determine the maximum number of enemies that can be killed by placing one bomb in an empty cell. The bomb eliminates all enemies in the same row and column from the placement point until it encounters a wall.
constraints: The rectangular grid has 1 to 500 rows and 1 to 500 columns; cells are exactly "0", "E", or "W".
Place one bomb only on "0". It kills enemies in four straight row/column rays, stopping at walls, not at enemies. Return 0 if there is no empty cell.
hints: Empty cells in the same wall-delimited segment see the same enemies along that direction.
Recompute a horizontal count only at a row segment start, and a vertical count only at a column segment start.
At each empty cell, combine its current row-segment count with its cached column-segment count.
Each segment is scanned once for its count and once during traversal, giving linear work in grid area.
editorial: Walls divide each row and column into independent segments. Keep a single horizontal count and one vertical count per column. When crossing a segment boundary, scan that segment to count enemies. At an empty cell the two counts add without double counting because the bomb cell is not an enemy. The independent oracle casts four rays separately from every empty cell.

tests.explanation: Bombing row 1, column 1 (zero-based) kills one enemy above, one below, and one left. The wall shields the enemy to its right; the maximum is 3.
Each empty cell sees exactly one enemy below. No bomb can kill all three because explosions do not turn corners.
